verses.zh: 当下，全会众大声喧嚷；那夜百姓都哭号。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Then all the community raised a loud cry,[NOTE:2] and the people wept[NOTE:3] that night.
notes: This chapter forms part of the story already begun. There are three major sections here: dissatisfaction with the reports (vv. 1-10), the threat of divine punishment (vv. 11-38), and the defeat of the Israelites (vv. 39-45). See K. D. Sakenfeld, “The Problem of Divine Forgiveness in Num 14, ” CBQ 37 (1975): 317-30; also J. R. Bartlett, “The Use of the Word רֹאשׁ as a Title in the Old Testament,” VT 19 (1969): 1-10.
The two verbs “lifted up their voice and cried” form a hendiadys; the idiom of raising the voice means that they cried aloud.

There are a number of things that the verb “to weep” or “wail” can connote. It could reflect joy, grief, lamentation, or repentance, but here it reflects fear, hopelessness, or vexation at the thought of coming all this way and being defeated by the Canaanite armies. See Judg 20:23, 26.

verses.zh: 以色列众人向摩西、亚伦发怨言；全会众对他们说：「巴不得我们早死在埃及地，或是死在这旷野。
verses.en: And all the Israelites murmured[NOTE:1] against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died[NOTE:2] in the land of Egypt, or if only we had perished[NOTE:3] in this wilderness!
notes: The Hebrew verb “to murmur” is לוּן (lun). It is a strong word, signifying far more than complaining or grumbling, as some of the modern translations have it. The word is most often connected to the wilderness experience. It is paralleled in the literature with the word “to rebel.” The murmuring is like a parliamentary vote of no confidence, for they no longer trusted their leaders and wished to choose a new leader and return. This “return to Egypt” becomes a symbol of their lack of faith in the Lord.

The optative is expressed by לוּ (lu) and then the verb, here the perfect tense מַתְנוּ (matnu)—“O that we had died….” Had they wanted to die in Egypt they should not have cried out to the Lord to deliver them from bondage. Here the people became consumed with the fear and worry of what lay ahead, and in their panic they revealed a lack of trust in God.
Heb “died.”

verses.zh: 耶和华为甚么把我们领到那地，使我们倒在刀下呢？我们的妻子和孩子必被掳掠。我们回埃及去岂不好吗？」
verses.en: Why has the Lord brought us into this land only to be killed by the sword, that our wives and our children should become plunder? Wouldn’t it be better for us to return to Egypt?”

verses.zh: 众人彼此说：「我们不如立一个首领回埃及去吧！」
verses.en: So they said to one another,[NOTE:1] “Let’s appoint[NOTE:2] a leader[NOTE:3] and return[NOTE:4] to Egypt.”
notes: Heb “a man to his brother.”
The verb is נָתַן (natan, “to give”), but this verb has quite a wide range of meanings in the Bible. Here it must mean “to make,” “to choose,” “to designate” or the like.

The word “head” (רֹאשׁ, roʾsh) probably refers to a tribal chief who was capable to judge and to lead to war (see J. R. Bartlett, “The Use of the Word רֹאשׁ as a Title in the Old Testament,” VT 19 [1969]: 1-10).
The form is a cohortative with a vav (ו) prefixed. After the preceding cohortative this could also be interpreted as a purpose or result clause—in order that we may return.

verses.zh: 摩西、亚伦就俯伏在以色列全会众面前。
verses.en: Then Moses and Aaron fell down with their faces to the ground[NOTE:1] before the whole assembled community[NOTE:2] of the Israelites.
notes: This action of Moses and Aaron is typical of them in the wilderness with the Israelites. The act shows self-abasement and deference before the sovereign Lord. They are not bowing before the people here, but in front of the people they bow before God. According to Num 16:41-50 this prostration is for the purpose of intercessory prayer. Here it prevents immediate wrath from God.
Heb “before all the assembly of the congregation.”

verses.zh: 窥探地的人中，嫩的儿子约书亚和耶孚尼的儿子迦勒撕裂衣服，
verses.en: And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of those who had investigated the land, tore their garments.

verses.zh: 对以色列全会众说：「我们所窥探、经过之地是极美之地。
verses.en: They said to the whole community of the Israelites, “The land we passed through to investigate is an exceedingly[NOTE:1] good land.
notes: The repetition of the adverb מְאֹד (meʾod) is used to express this: “very, very [good].”

verses.zh: 耶和华若喜悦我们，就必将我们领进那地，把地赐给我们；那地原是流奶与蜜之地。
verses.en: If the Lord delights in us, then he will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land that is flowing with milk and honey.[NOTE:1]
notes: The subjective genitives “milk and honey” are symbols of the wealth of the land, second only to bread. Milk was a sign of such abundance (Gen 49:12; Isa 7:21, 22). Because of the climate the milk would thicken quickly and become curds, eaten with bread or turned into butter. The honey mentioned here is the wild honey (see Deut 32:13; Judg 14:8-9). It signified sweetness, or the finer things of life (Ezek 3:3).

verses.zh: 但你们不可背叛耶和华，也不要怕那地的居民；因为他们是我们的食物，并且荫庇他们的已经离开他们。有耶和华与我们同在，不要怕他们！」
verses.en: Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us.[NOTE:1] Their protection[NOTE:2] has turned aside from them, but the Lord is with us. Do not fear them!”
notes: The expression must indicate that they could destroy the enemies as easily as they could eat bread.
Heb “their shade.” The figure compares the shade from the sun with the protection from the enemy. It is also possible that the text is alluding to their deities here.

verses.zh: 但全会众说：「拿石头打死他们二人。」忽然，耶和华的荣光在会幕中向以色列众人显现。
verses.en: However, the whole community threatened to stone them.[NOTE:1] But[NOTE:2] the glory[NOTE:3] of the Lord appeared to all the Israelites at the tent[NOTE:4] of meeting.
notes: Heb “said to stone them with stones.” The verb and the object are not from the same root, but the combination nonetheless forms an emphasis equal to the cognate accusative.
The vav (ו) on the noun “glory” indicates a strong contrast, one that interrupts their threatened attack.

The glory of the Lord refers to the reality of the Lord’s presence in a manifestation of his power and splendor. It showed to all that God was a living God. The appearance of the glory indicated blessing for the obedient, but disaster for the disobedient.
The Greek, Syriac, and Tg. Ps.-J. have “in the cloud over the tent.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「这百姓藐视我要到几时呢？我在他们中间行了这一切神迹，他们还不信我要到几时呢？
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “How long will this people despise[NOTE:1] me, and how long will they not believe[NOTE:2] in me, in spite of the signs that I have done among them?
notes: The verb נָאַץ (naʾats) means “to condemn, spurn” (BDB 610 s.v.). Coats suggests that in some contexts the word means actual rejection or renunciation (Rebellion in the Wilderness, 146, 7). This would include the idea of distaste.

The verb “to believe” (root אָמַן, ʾaman) has the basic idea of support, dependability for the root. The Hiphil has a declarative sense, namely, to consider something reliable or dependable and to act on it. The people did not trust what the Lord said.

verses.zh: 我要用瘟疫击杀他们，使他们不得承受那地，叫你的后裔成为大国，比他们强胜。」
verses.en: I will strike them with the pestilence,[NOTE:1] and I will disinherit them—I will make you into a nation that is greater and mightier than they!”
notes: The Greek version has “death.”

verses.zh: 摩西对耶和华说：「埃及人必听见这事；因为你曾施展大能，将这百姓从他们中间领上来。
verses.en: Moses said to the Lord, “When the Egyptians hear[NOTE:1] it—for you brought up this people by your power from among them—
notes: The construction is unusual in that we have here a perfect tense with a vav (ו) consecutive with no verb before it to establish the time sequence. The context requires that this be taken as a vav (ו) consecutive. It actually forms the protasis for the next verse, and would best be rendered “when…then they will say.”

verses.zh: 埃及人要将这事传给迦南地的居民；那民已经听见你―耶和华是在这百姓中间；因为你面对面被人看见，有你的云彩停在他们以上。你日间在云柱中，夜间在火柱中，在他们前面行。
verses.en: then they will tell it to the inhabitants[NOTE:1] of this land. They have heard that you, Lord, are among this people, that you, Lord, are seen face to face,[NOTE:2] that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them by day in a pillar of cloud and in a pillar of fire by night.
notes: The singular participle is to be taken here as a collective, representing all the inhabitants of the land.
“Face-to-face” is literally “eye to eye.” It only occurs elsewhere in Isa 52:8. This expresses the closest communication possible.

verses.zh: 如今你若把这百姓杀了，如杀一人，那些听见你名声的列邦必议论说：
verses.en: If you kill[NOTE:1] this entire people at once,[NOTE:2] then the nations that have heard of your fame will say,
notes: The verb is the Hiphil perfect of מוּת (mut), וְהֵמַתָּה (vehemattah). The vav (ו) consecutive makes this also a future time sequence verb, but again in a conditional clause.
Heb “as one man.”

verses.zh: 『耶和华因为不能把这百姓领进他向他们起誓应许之地，所以在旷野把他们杀了。』
verses.en: ‘Because the Lord was not able to bring this people into the land that he swore to them, he killed them in the wilderness.’

verses.zh: 现在求主大显能力，照你所说过的话说：
verses.en: So now, let the power of my Lord[NOTE:1] be great, just as you have said,
notes: The form in the text is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay), the word that is usually used in place of the tetragrammaton. It is the plural form with the pronominal suffix, and so must refer to God.

verses.zh: 『耶和华不轻易发怒，并有丰盛的慈爱，赦免罪孽和过犯；万不以有罪的为无罪，必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三、四代。』
verses.en: ‘The Lord is slow to anger and abounding in loyal love,[NOTE:1] forgiving iniquity and transgression,[NOTE:2] but by no means clearing the guilty,[NOTE:3] visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children until the third and fourth generations.’[NOTE:4]
notes: The expression רַב־חֶסֶד (rav khesed) means “much of loyal love” or “faithful love.” Some have it “totally faithful,” but that omits the aspect of his love.
Or “rebellion.”

The infinitive absolute emphasizes the verbal activity of the imperfect tense, which here serves as a habitual imperfect. Negated it states what God does not do; and the infinitive makes that certain.
The Decalogue adds “to those who hate me.” The point of the line is that the effects of sin, if not the sinful traits themselves, are passed on to the next generation.

verses.zh: 求你照你的大慈爱赦免这百姓的罪孽，好像你从埃及到如今常赦免他们一样。」
verses.en: Please forgive[NOTE:1] the iniquity of this people according to your great loyal love,[NOTE:2] just as you have forgiven this people from Egypt even until now.”
notes: The verb סְלַח־נָא (selakh naʾ), the imperative form, means “forgive” (see Ps 130:4), “pardon,” “excuse.” The imperative is of course a prayer, a desire, and not a command.
The construct unit is “the greatness of your loyal love.” This is the genitive of specification, the first word being the modifier.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「我照着你的话赦免了他们。
verses.en: Then the Lord said, “I have forgiven them as you asked.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “forgiven according to your word.” The direct object, “them,” is implied.

verses.zh: 然我指着我的永生起誓，遍地要被我的荣耀充满。
verses.en: But truly, as I live,[NOTE:1] all the earth will be filled with the glory of the Lord.
notes: This is the oath formula, but in the Pentateuch it occurs here and in v. 28.

verses.zh: 这些人虽看见我的荣耀和我在埃及与旷野所行的神迹，仍然试探我这十次，不听从我的话，
verses.en: For all the people have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have tempted[NOTE:1] me now these ten times,[NOTE:2] and have not obeyed me[NOTE:3]—
notes: The verb נָסָה (nasah) means “to test, to tempt, to prove.” It can be used to indicate things are tried or proven, or for testing in a good sense, or tempting in the bad sense, i.e., putting God to the test. In all uses there is uncertainty or doubt about the outcome. Some uses of the verb are positive: If God tests Abraham in Genesis 22:1, it is because there is uncertainty whether he fears the Lord or not; if people like Gideon put out the fleece and test the Lord, it is done by faith but in order to be certain of the Lord’s presence. But here, when these people put God to the test ten times, it was because they doubted the goodness and ability of God, and this was a major weakness. They had proof to the contrary, but chose to challenge God.
“Ten” is here a round figure, emphasizing the complete testing. But see F. V. Winnett, The Mosaic Tradition, 121-54.
Heb “listened to my voice.”

verses.zh: 他们断不得看见我向他们的祖宗所起誓应许之地。凡藐视我的，一个也不得看见；
verses.en: they will by no means[NOTE:1] see the land that I promised on oath to their fathers, nor will any of them who despised me see it—
notes: The word אִם (ʾim) indicates a negative oath formula: “if” means “they will not.” It is elliptical. In a human oath one would be saying: “The Lord do to me if they see…,” meaning “they will by no means see.” Here God is swearing that they will not see the land.

verses.zh: 惟独我的仆人迦勒，因他另有一个心志，专一跟从我，我就把他领进他所去过的那地；他的后裔也必得那地为业。
verses.en: Only my servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit and has followed me fully—I will bring him into the land where he had gone, and his descendants[NOTE:1] will possess it.
notes: Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 亚玛力人和迦南人住在谷中，明天你们要转回，从红海的路往旷野去。」
verses.en: (Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites were living in the valleys.)[NOTE:1] Tomorrow, turn and journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.”
notes: The judgment on Israel is that they turn back to the desert and not attack the tribes in the land. So a parenthetical clause is inserted to state who was living there. They would surely block the entrance to the land from the south—unless God removed them. And he is not going to do that for Israel.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron:

verses.zh: 「这恶会众向我发怨言，我忍耐他们要到几时呢？以色列人向我所发的怨言，我都听见了。
verses.en: “How long must I bear[NOTE:1] with this evil congregation[NOTE:2] that murmurs against me? I have heard the complaints of the Israelites that they murmured against me.
notes: The figure is aposiopesis, or sudden silence. The main verb is deleted from the line, “how long…this evil community.” The intensity of the emotion is the reason for the ellipsis.

It is worth mentioning in passing that this is one of the Rabbinic proof texts for having at least ten men to form a congregation and have prayer. If God called ten men (the bad spies) a “congregation,” then a congregation must have ten men. But here the word “community/congregation” refers in this context to the people of Israel as a whole, not just to the ten spies.

verses.zh: 你们告诉他们，耶和华说：『我指着我的永生起誓，我必要照你们达到我耳中的话待你们。
verses.en: Say to them, ‘As I live,[NOTE:1] says[NOTE:2] the Lord, I will surely do to you just what you have spoken in my hearing.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here again is the oath that God swore in his wrath, an oath he swore by himself, that they would not enter the land. “As the Lord lives,” or “by the life of the Lord,” are ways to render it.
The word נְאֻם (neʾum) is an “oracle.” It is followed by the subjective genitive: “the oracle of the Lord” is equal to saying “the Lord says.”

Heb “in my ears.”sn They had expressed the longing to have died in the wilderness, and not in war. God will now give them that. They would not say to God “your will be done,” so he says to them, “your will be done” (to borrow from C. S. Lewis).

verses.zh: 你们的尸首必倒在这旷野，并且你们中间凡被数点、从二十岁以外、向我发怨言的，
verses.en: Your dead bodies[NOTE:1] will fall in this wilderness—all those of you who were numbered, according to your full number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me.
notes: Or “your corpses” (also in vv. 32, 33).

verses.zh: 必不得进我起誓应许叫你们住的那地；惟有耶孚尼的儿子迦勒和嫩的儿子约书亚才能进去。
verses.en: You will by no means enter into the land where[NOTE:1] I swore[NOTE:2] to settle[NOTE:3] you. The only exceptions are Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
notes: The relative pronoun “which” is joined with the resumptive pronoun “in it” to form a smoother reading “where.”
The Hebrew text uses the anthropomorphic expression “I raised my hand” in taking an oath.
Heb “to cause you to dwell; to cause you to settle.”

verses.zh: 但你们的妇人孩子，就是你们所说、要被掳掠的，我必把他们领进去，他们就得知你们所厌弃的那地。
verses.en: But I will bring in your little ones, whom you said would become victims of war,[NOTE:1] and they will enjoy[NOTE:2] the land that you have despised.
notes: Or “plunder.”
Heb “know.”

verses.zh: 至于你们，你们的尸首必倒在这旷野；
verses.en: But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness,

verses.zh: 你们的儿女必在旷野飘流四十年，担当你们淫行的罪，直到你们的尸首在旷野消灭。
verses.en: and your children will wander[NOTE:1] in the wilderness 40 years and suffer for your unfaithfulness,[NOTE:2] until your dead bodies lie finished[NOTE:3] in the wilderness.
notes: The word is “shepherds.” It means that the people would be wilderness nomads, grazing their flock on available land.

Heb “you shall bear your whoredoms.” The imagery of prostitution is used throughout the Bible to reflect spiritual unfaithfulness, leaving the covenant relationship and following after false gods. Here it is used generally for their rebellion in the wilderness, but not for following other gods.

The infinitive is from תָּמַם (tamam), which means “to be complete.” The word is often used to express completeness in a good sense—whole, blameless, or the like. Here and in v. 35 it seems to mean “until your deaths have been completed.” See also Gen 47:15; Deut 2:15.

verses.zh: 按你们窥探那地的四十日，一年顶一日，你们要担当罪孽四十年，就知道我与你们疏远了，
verses.en: According to the number of the days you have investigated this land, 40 days—one day for a year—you will suffer for[NOTE:1] your iniquities, 40 years, and you will know what it means to thwart me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you shall bear.”

The phrase refers to the consequences of open hostility to God, or perhaps abandonment of God. The noun תְּנוּאָה (tenuʾah) occurs in Job 33:10 (perhaps). The related verb occurs in Num 30:6 HT (30:5 ET) and 32:7 with the sense of “disallow, discourage.” The sense of the expression adopted in this translation comes from the meticulous study of R. Loewe, “Divine Frustration Exegetically Frustrated,” Words and Meanings, 137-58.

verses.zh: 我―耶和华说过，我总要这样待这一切聚集敌我的恶会众；他们必在这旷野消灭，在这里死亡。』」
verses.en: I, the Lord, have said, “I will surely do so to all this evil congregation that has gathered together against me. In this wilderness they will be finished, and there they will die!”’”

verses.zh: 摩西所打发、窥探那地的人回来，报那地的恶信，叫全会众向摩西发怨言，
verses.en: The men whom Moses sent to investigate the land, who returned and made the whole community murmur against him by producing[NOTE:1] an evil report about the land,
notes: The verb is the Hiphil infinitive construct with a ל (lamed) preposition from the root יָצָא (yatsaʾ, “to bring out”). The use of the infinitive here is epexegetical, that is, explaining how they caused the people to murmur.

verses.zh: 这些报恶信的人都遭瘟疫，死在耶和华面前。
verses.en: those men who produced the evil report about the land, died by the plague before the Lord.

verses.zh: 其中惟有嫩的儿子约书亚和耶孚尼的儿子迦勒仍然存活。
verses.en: But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among[NOTE:1] the men who went to investigate the land, lived.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the preposition “from,” “some of”—“from those men.” The relative pronoun is added to make a smoother reading.

verses.zh: 摩西将这些话告诉以色列众人，他们就甚悲哀。
verses.en: When Moses told[NOTE:1] these things to all the Israelites, the people mourned[NOTE:2] greatly.
notes: The preterite here is subordinated to the next preterite to form a temporal clause.
The word אָבַל (ʾaval) is rare, used mostly for mourning over deaths, but it is used here of mourning over bad news (see also Exod 33:4; 1 Sam 15:35; 16:1; etc.).

verses.zh: 清早起来，上山顶去，说：「我们在这里，我们有罪了；情愿上耶和华所应许的地方去。」
verses.en: And early[NOTE:1] in the morning they went up to the crest of the hill country,[NOTE:2] saying, “Here we are, and we will go up to the place that the Lord commanded,[NOTE:3] for we have sinned.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The verb וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ (vayyashkimu) is often found in a verbal hendiadys construction: “They rose early…and they went up” means “they went up early.”
The Hebrew text says literally “the top of the hill,” but judging from the location and the terrain it probably means the heights of the hill country.
The verb is simply “said,” but it means the place that the Lord said to go up to in order to fight.

Their sin was unbelief. They could have gone and conquered the area if they had trusted the Lord for their victory. They did not, and so they were condemned to perish in the wilderness. Now, thinking that by going they can undo all that, they plan to go. But this is also disobedience, for the Lord said they would not now take the land, and yet they think they can. Here is their second sin, presumption.

verses.zh: 摩西说：「你们为何违背耶和华的命令呢？这事不能顺利了。
verses.en: But Moses said, “Why[NOTE:1] are you now transgressing the commandment[NOTE:2] of the Lord? It will not succeed!
notes: The line literally has, “Why is this [that] you are transgressing….” The demonstrative pronoun is enclitic; it brings the force of “why in the world are you doing this now?”
Heb “mouth.”

verses.zh: 不要上去；因为耶和华不在你们中间，恐怕你们被仇敌杀败了。
verses.en: Do not go up, for the Lord is not among you, and you will be[NOTE:1] defeated before your enemies.
notes: This verb could also be subordinated to the preceding: “that you be not smitten.”

verses.zh: 亚玛力人和迦南人都在你们面前，你们必倒在刀下；因你们退回不跟从耶和华，所以他必不与你们同在。」
verses.en: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the Lord, the Lord will not be with you.”

verses.zh: 他们却擅敢上山顶去，然而耶和华的约柜和摩西没有出营。
verses.en: But they dared[NOTE:1] to go up to the crest of the hill, although[NOTE:2] neither the ark of the covenant of the Lord nor Moses departed from the camp.
notes: N. H. Snaith compares Arabic ʿafala (“to swell”) and gafala (“reckless, headstrong”; Leviticus and Numbers [NCB], 248). The word עֹפֶל (ʿofel) means a “rounded hill” or a “tumor.” The idea behind the verb may be that of “swelling,” and so “act presumptuously.”
The disjunctive vav (ו) here introduces a circumstantial clause; the most appropriate one here would be the concessive “although.”

verses.zh: 于是亚玛力人和住在那山上的迦南人都下来击打他们，把他们杀退了，直到何珥玛。
verses.en: So the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country swooped down[NOTE:1] and attacked them[NOTE:2] as far as Hormah.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “came down.”
The verb used here means “crush by beating,” or “pounded” them. The Greek text used “cut them in pieces.”
The name “Hormah” means “destruction”; it is from the word that means “ban, devote” for either destruction or temple use.
